hypothesis: Catastrophic MTS drawdowns arise because many otherwise-profitable signals enter close together during dislocation and experience correlated adverse excursions before recovery; portfolio-level timing/overlap, not simply bad signal expectancy, creates the large drawdown.
portfolio_mechanics: Reuse run_discovery_portfolio_capital_stage1_portfolio build_events/simulate assumptions: next-session-open entry, close marking, nonlevered cash limited equal sizing, base trade fraction=1/median concurrency.
frozen_metrics: fraction active currently underwater vs entry
mean current PnL of active positions
within each collapse local portfolio peak/trough drawdown using equal-weight nonlevered portfolio
at each collapse trough: active count, underwater fraction, eventual-winner fraction, eventual winners currently underwater, eventual winners down >=5%/10%
terminal-winner MAE distribution inside collapse vs controls
share of collapse terminal winners that first suffered >=5%/10%/20% MAE

interpretation.strong_support: collapse troughs show broad simultaneous underwater exposure while a substantial share of those same active positions later finish profitable, plus collapse-period terminal winners commonly suffer meaningful MAE before recovery
interpretation.refute: collapse trough exposure is dominated by trades that ultimately remain losers, with little evidence of profitable trades suffering synchronized temporary drawdowns

prohibitions: no threshold search beyond frozen descriptive 5/10/20 percent diagnostics
